translation_direction: de → vi; direct from the specifically identified complete German electronic witness
ai_disclosure: Direct AI-produced Vietnamese prose by Claude Opus 5.5. The drafting system conducted the final full assessment; a separate-context assessment by the same model family read every pair and supplied findings first. No human translator, editor, reviewer, independent model consensus or actual reader feedback is recorded.

entry_conditions: Complete named-source and Vietnamese texts, explicit alignment and exact content hashes.
Compare every source and target passage; disclose that this assessor also revised the text and has seen earlier AI assessments.
Source and target edition titles are present and compared explicitly; the title review must match both catalog title strings exactly.
exit_conditions: One complete AI review with a weighted score at least 8.6 using the five unchanged weights and half-point category scores; no separate numerical dimension floors.
All canonical passages reviewed; no unresolved major or critical finding; source and target hashes match the final text.
Publication and rights status are recorded separately in the edition catalog; an AI score does not supply a license.
The selected review includes source_title, target_title and a substantive title rationale; changed titles require a fresh matching review.
review_process.human_feedback: Optional after publication or while a work remains a draft; no prior human publication review is required by v2.

decisions.decision: Kleist’s cold, breathless, legalistic chronicle voice is kept with the very long periods intact, one paragraph per unit, and no explanatory padding.
decisions.rationale: The horror is in the facts, told in single breaths.

decisions.decision: The German text comes from Project Gutenberg #6645 because de.wikisource has no accessible copy; it is translated directly from the German, not from an English version.

revision_history.scope: Complete initial direct translation, separate-context full source/target assessment and concrete revisions before the selected final review.

changes.explanation: ‘Sicherheit für zukünftige … seinen Mitbürgern’ was rendered in garbled Vietnamese; now ‘sự bảo đảm trước những xúc phạm về sau’ for his fellow citizens.

‘Der’ (the look) was read as the Junker in the sentence about a look that would have crushed him; first the referent of ‘không biết mặt’ was wrong, then the pronoun of the look was inverted; both corrected (the second after the last blind review).
A clause about the horse dealer’s disgust was duplicated from a revision; removed.
The clause on Kohlhaas’s aversion to making common cause with Nagelschmidt was garbled; rewritten.
‘Seiner Milde ungeachtet’ (despite its mildness) was reversed into ‘despite its severity’; corrected.
The chancellor’s office was rendered two ways in units 31, 32, 35 and 37; now ‘Đại pháp quan’ and ‘Phủ Đại pháp quan’ throughout.
The Goldwaage-like sense of justice clause in unit 4 was garbled (‘ông chưa chắc là một tội lỗi…’), found in the second review; rewritten after that review.

selection_limit: Chosen for a complete, directly sourced and openly reusable Vietnamese edition. Existing Vietnamese translations, their quality and reader demand have not been comprehensively assessed; no absence or superiority claim is made.

glossary.draft_rendering: Đại pháp quan / Phủ Đại pháp quan
glossary.rationale: One rendering for the Saxon chancellor and his office.
The prince of the house of Meissen.
The knacker who holds the horses.
The sermon-like letter keeps its own archaic weight.

witness_decision: Selected Project Gutenberg #6645, an electronic transcription of Heinrich von Kleist’s Ausgewählte Schriften, taking only Michael Kohlhaas, the last work in the volume; the Gutenberg page does not name the exact printing and the text was not collated with the 1810 first printing.

unresolved_questions.explanation: ‘Erzkanzler’ is rendered ‘Đại pháp quan’ where the glossary asks for ‘Tổng pháp quan’.
‘Vành móng ngựa’ for ‘vor den Schranken’ is a modern courtroom idiom.
‘Hauptmann’ and the town councillors are rendered with slightly anachronistic words.
‘Khuya sáng hôm sau’ does not fit ‘spät am andern Morgen’.

title_review.rationale: The title is the hero’s name; no earlier Vietnamese title was checked.

passage_assessment_notes.assessment: The opening: a horse dealer on the Havel in the middle of the sixteenth century, ‘one of the most upright and at the same time most terrible men of his time’.
The last unit: the last of Kohlhaas’s descendants in the previous century.
